source.title: Neural Scaling Laws of Deep ReLU and Deep Operator Network: A Theoretical Study
source.authors: Hao Liu; Ze-Cheng Zhang; Wen-Jing Liao; Hayden Schaeffer

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper derives scaling bounds for DeepONet operator learning, a different setting from language-model pretraining, using theoretical approximation and generalization analyses.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own theoretical bounds for DeepONet approximation and generalization errors. Cited empirical scaling results from other studies are not recorded as rows. It does not test language models, held-out cross-entropy, compute-optimal allocations, downstream tasks, or architectural shape effects.
record.test_reason: The paper is purely theoretical. It proves upper bounds on DeepONet approximation and generalization error as functions of parameter count and sample count, under assumptions such as Lipschitz operators and a bounded network class. It runs no experiments and measures no loss. An upper bound cannot show that real loss follows, or fails to follow, a power law. The authors themselves treat empirical power laws (Lu et al. 2021b; de Hoop et al. 2022) as given and offer their bounds as a partial explanation. They do not test them. So no version is tested. The record's 'tests/T3' with V5 labels should be dropped.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors derive upper bounds that partially explain neural scaling laws of DeepONet: slow logarithmic-type rates for general Lipschitz operators, and power-law rates when input functions lie in a finite-dimensional linear subspace. They add that the results also hold for deep ReLU and similar networks, and that optimality of the bounds is left open.
record.recipe_differences: The study derives mathematical bounds for DeepONet operator learning; it does not run language-model scaling experiments or measure held-out cross-entropy.
record.method_sensitivity: The derived rates differ between the general setting and the setting with finite-dimensional linear structure in the input functions.

fits_no_version.finding: Proved upper bounds for DeepONet (and deep ReLU networks) learning Lipschitz operators. Without input structure, error is at most order (log N#/log log N#)^(-1/d1) in parameters and (log n/log log n)^(-2/d1) in samples. With inputs in a bU-dimensional linear subspace, the bounds become power laws: N#^(-1/(bU+d2)) and n^(-2/(2+bU+d2)) log^3 n.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Theoretical approximation and generalization upper bounds for neural operators decay as power laws in model and data size only when input functions have low-dimensional structure.

record.problems: The evidence consists of theoretical upper bounds for a different model class and task, not empirical loss measurements. The power-law results require a specific low-dimensional input assumption, and the paper does not test language-model pretraining or compute-optimal allocation.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported qualifying scaling bounds relevant to V5 were left out.

untested.parts: No empirical loss curves for operator learning or any other modality or regime. Only theoretical upper bounds are given.
Not addressed; architecture is set by the proof construction, and shape effects at fixed size are not studied.
Not addressed empirically. Different bound rates under different assumptions are not fitted exponents.

record.verdict_notes: R3's exponent in the record (bU/(1+d2)) appears mis-transcribed. The text's Table 1 and Theorem 3 discussion give approximation error of order N#^(-1/(bU+d2)). The study is a preprint with no experiments.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss and its scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run losses from power-law fits to smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocations and their dependence on compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
The paper studies theoretical operator-learning error bounds, not empirical pretraining loss. It does not test image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Downstream task performance and its predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits on fitting choices, and empirical departures from single power laws.

rows.measure: Theoretical approximation error as a function of network parameter count N#.
rows.locator: Section 4.2, Theorem 1 and Model scaling law discussion
rows.note: This is a derived upper-rate result, not an empirical measurement of test loss. The authors characterize the general-case convergence as very slow.
rows.check: Theoretical upper bound on approximation error (Theorem 1/Corollary 1), not a measured loss. A slow log-rate upper bound does not show actual error scales slowly, so it cannot bear on V5. 'partial' is not justified.
